record.paper_title: Infinity in string cosmology: A review through open problems
record.context_brief: Interacting fluids in flat string cosmology
record.original_question: How do the known single-fluid asymptotic results for flat string cosmologies change when the matter sector is replaced by two interacting, fairly general fluids that exchange energy, and which conclusions about the physical viability of string cosmology survive in that more general interacting setting?

evidence.quote:
3.3 Interacting ﬂuids in ﬂat string cosmology
The aim of this project is to examine how all known single ﬂuid results in ﬂat string cosmologies generalize to the case of two interacting, more or less general ﬂuids which exchange energy. This is very important because it will reveal which results remain in such a generalized situation, thus oﬀering another clue to the physical viability of string cosmology.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a spatially flat Friedmann–Lemaître–Robertson–Walker string cosmology in the string frame, governed by the tree-level (lowest-order in α′) effective equations of motion derived from the dilaton-gravity action

  S = ∫ d^(n+1)x √(-g) e^(-φ) [ R + (∂φ)^2 - 2 Λ ] + S_matter,

with scale factor a(t), shifted dilaton φ̄ = φ - n ln a, and matter sector consisting of two perfect fluids labelled i = 1, 2 with energy densities ρ_i, pressures p_i = w_i ρ_i (with constants w_i, or more generally barotropic equations of state), interacting via an energy-exchange term Q(t):

  ρ̇_1 + n H (ρ_1 + p_1) = -Q,
  ρ̇_2 + n H (ρ_2 + p_2) = +Q,

coupled to the string-frame field equations
  n(n-1) H^2 - 2 n H φ̄˙ + φ̄˙^2 - 2 Λ = 2 e^φ̄ (ρ_1 + ρ_2),
  (other dilaton-gravity equations as derived from S),
where H = ȧ/a.

(a) Determine the asymptotic behaviour (as t → ±∞ or as one approaches a curvature/dilaton singularity) of the solutions (a(t), φ(t), ρ_1(t), ρ_2(t)) in the pre-big-bang and post-big-bang branches, generalising the known single-fluid asymptotic results to this two-fluid interacting setting, for a representative class of interaction terms Q (e.g. Q = α H ρ_1 + β H ρ_2, or Q proportional to ρ̇_total, with α, β real constants).

(b) Identify which qualitative conclusions established in the single-fluid case—such as the existence of a graceful exit from the pre- to post-big-bang phase, avoidance or persistence of curvature/dilaton singularities, scale-factor duality behaviour, and stability of attractor solutions—remain valid when the matter sector is replaced by two interacting fluids exchanging energy.

State precisely the asymptotic regimes (fixed points, scaling solutions, late- and early-time limits) and prove which of the single-fluid viability features survive in the interacting two-fluid generalisation.
artifact.status_search_result: No specific resolution of this two-interacting-fluid generalisation of flat string cosmology asymptotics could be verified. The question is posed as a research project whose status is not clearly settled in the accessible literature.
